rules.statement: Build a client connection from its separate parts with the client library's typed options or builder (for example StackExchange.Redis `ConfigurationOptions` or `NpgsqlConnectionStringBuilder`), and never by concatenating or substituting a secret into a connection-string text.
rules.why: Text splicing lets a password that contains `,` or `=` change what the connection string means. A typed options object keeps each value as a value.
rules.check: Look for string interpolation, concatenation, string.Format or `$(VAR)` expansion that puts a host, user or password into a connection string. The code should set the properties of an options or builder object instead.

rules.statement: When a setting can be configured in two alternative forms (for example a section of parts or a finished connection string), refuse at startup a configuration that sets both forms, or that leaves out a required part, instead of silently choosing one.
rules.why: A mixed or incomplete configuration should stop the host at start, the same way the deployment chart refuses it at render time.
rules.check: Look at the resolver code for alternative configuration forms. Check that it throws when both forms are present and when a required part such as Host is missing, and that it does not quietly prefer one form.

rules.statement: Validate each connection part's range and type at startup (for example a port within 1-65535 and a boolean TLS flag), and bind the section strictly so that a misspelled key fails.
rules.why: A misspelled or invalid part must stop the host at start instead of being ignored.
rules.check: Look at new connection or options sections. Check that they bind with unknown keys rejected, and that the port range and boolean parsing are checked when the host starts.

rules.statement: Configuration validation error messages name the configuration path that failed and never include the configured value.
rules.why: A configured value can be a secret such as a password, and error messages end up in logs.
rules.check: Look at the exception messages thrown by configuration validation. Flag any message that interpolates the bound value instead of the key path only.

rules.statement: In a Helm chart, pass each part of an operator-owned credential to the pods as an environment variable from a `secretKeyRef` on the operator's Secret, and do not copy it into a chart-made Secret through `lookup` or a hook.
rules.why: A copy goes stale when the operator rotates the password, and `lookup` returns nothing under `helm template` and Argo CD, so the chart would render differently from how it installs.
rules.check: Look in chart templates for `lookup` calls on Secrets, for hooks that copy Secret data, and for templates that assemble credentials into a new Secret.

rules.statement: In a Helm chart, fail the render (for example with `fail`) when the values configure a connection in two conflicting forms, or name a parts Secret without the required host key.
rules.why: The chart should refuse an unusable release at render time instead of deploying pods that cannot connect.
rules.check: Look at new chart values that offer alternative connection forms. Check that the templates add `fail` guards for the case where both are set and for missing required keys.
